questions.question: A laboratory has purchased a new pH meter. How should it be handled under <1058>?

options.A: Classify as Group A; only observe that it functions properly, with no further confirmation
options.B: Classify as Group B and perform full software validation and all IQ/OQ/PQ items
options.C: Classify as Group C; all qualification elements, including software validation, must be considered
options.D: Classify as Group B; perform routine calibration, maintenance, or performance checks depending on the criticality of the use

questions.explanation: A pH meter, like an oven, is a Group B instrument. Such instruments may provide measurements or control experimental conditions that affect measurements, so proper functioning typically requires only routine calibration, maintenance, or performance checks, to a degree that depends on the criticality of the application. They usually have only firmware and no user-updatable software. Group A covers instruments with no measurement capability, while Group C covers highly computerized, complex instruments such as HPLC.

questions.question: Comparing OQ and PQ, which statement is correct?

options.A: OQ verifies that the instrument as shipped meets its design; PQ verifies that the laboratory environment meets specifications
options.B: OQ demonstrates that the instrument operates correctly in the user's environment per the URS; PQ demonstrates continued compliance under actual conditions of use
options.C: OQ can be replaced by testing of routine analytical samples; PQ is performed only once when installation is complete
options.D: OQ and PQ must have exactly the same test items, and their specifications may not be set differently

questions.explanation: OQ verifies that the instrument operates correctly in the user's environment according to the specifications in the URS; routine analytical testing is not equivalent to OQ. PQ demonstrates that the instrument continues to meet the user-defined specifications under actual conditions of use; after IQ and OQ are completed, its fitness for use is shown by ongoing PQ. PQ tests may resemble OQ tests, but the specifications can differ.
questions.reference: USP <1058> Analytical Instrument Qualification › Analytical Instrument Qualification Process › Qualification Phases; Operational Qualification; Performance Qualification

questions.question: What is the position of <1058> on the firmware of computerized analytical instruments?

options.A: It is considered part of the instrument and needs no separate on-site qualification, but the version should be recorded in the IQ
options.B: It requires its own full on-site software qualification, approved separately from the instrument qualification, before use
options.C: The firmware version need not be recorded or placed under change control, because users usually cannot modify it
options.D: It needs qualification only when the user defines programs on the instrument; otherwise no information needs to be recorded

questions.explanation: Firmware is considered part of the instrument itself. When the instrument is qualified at the user's site, the firmware is essentially qualified as well, so no separate on-site qualification is needed. Where possible, the firmware version should be recorded in the IQ, and version changes are tracked through the instrument's change control. In addition, fixed firmware calculations and user-defined programs must be validated by the user.
questions.reference: USP <1058> Analytical Instrument Qualification › Software Validation › Firmware

questions.question: A qualified instrument has undergone a major repair. Which of the following best matches the requirements of <1058>?

options.A: The repair may be done by the supplier, and the user needs no assessment or documented record
options.B: As long as the supplier provides a shipping inspection report, the instrument may return to use immediately after the repair
options.C: Assess through change control and repeat the relevant IQ, OQ, and/or PQ tests
options.D: DQ and all IQ/OQ/PQ must always be repeated, regardless of the scope of the repair

questions.explanation: After a major repair or modification, the instrument should be assessed through change control, and the relevant IQ, OQ, and/or PQ tests should be repeated to demonstrate that it still operates satisfactorily. Everything does not always have to be repeated, but the instrument also cannot return to use without assessment.
questions.reference: USP <1058> Analytical Instrument Qualification › Analytical Instrument Qualification Process › Qualification Phases

questions.question: A laboratory purchased an OQ test package from a supplier and the supplier performed it. Under <1058>, what is the user's responsibility?

options.A: The supplier bears full responsibility; the user only needs to file it, without reviewing the test content or result data
options.B: The user only needs to confirm that the supplier signed it, without examining whether the tests are scientifically sound
options.C: The quality unit takes over final responsibility, and the user merely supplies the usage requirements
options.D: The user must review its soundness before execution and approve it afterward; final responsibility rests with the user

questions.explanation: For an OQ test package purchased from a service provider, the user must review it to ensure the tests are scientifically sound and compliant with regulations, reviewing the documents before execution and approving them afterward to ensure completeness and accuracy. Consultants and suppliers may assist, but final responsibility for instrument qualification rests with the user.
questions.reference: USP <1058> Analytical Instrument Qualification › Operational Qualification; Roles and Responsibilities › Users
